label: rem:substrate-telescope
title: Substrate Telescopes
html: The directional dependence of q-torsion suggests a new class of detector: the Substrate Telescope. A large, high-purity single crystal is slowly rotated while the variation of vacuum noise power or phonon resonance efficiency is recorded as a function of orientation. The q-torsion leaves carry a preferred direction inherited from the q-deformed Reeb flow (q-Reeb flow). Consequently, the noise spectrum should exhibit a modulation correlated with the crystal's orientation relative to the bulk bundle. Analogous to a Weber-bar gravitational wave detector, this instrument targets the anisotropy of the substrate parameter rather than metric strain.
